title: Jane Doe at centre of Cornell rape case targeted with threats, her lawyer says
summary: The woman who has alleged she was drugged and raped by ‌Cornell University students has been the target of threats, her lawyer said on Sunday.

image.caption: Students walk past the entrance of Cornell University in Ithaca, N.Y., on Thursday. (Lauren Petracca/Reuters)

blocks.text: The woman who has alleged she was drugged and raped by ‌Cornell University students has been the target of threats, her lawyer said on Sunday.
Cornell under scrutiny following outcry over university's handling of allegations

Thomas Giuffra, who represents the woman identified as Jane Doe, told CNN that people have threatened to silence or harm her if she does not withdraw her civil lawsuit alleging that several members of a Cornell fraternity drugged and ​raped her in 2024.
"She's received multiple threats," Giuffra said on CNN's State ​of the Union, adding that he had also been threatened.

"I'm not afraid of these people," he said. "But the threats, the abuse to protect what's going on, the status quo — these guys are ​disgusting. They should stay in their mother's basement and stay out of the world."

The identity of ⁠Jane Doe has become ⁠part of the fevered online conversation surrounding the case. Women ‌on social media have been posting #IamJaneDoe in solidarity with the accuser and to counter some who have sought to publicly name her.
Advocate calls for 'overhaul' of student groups to address harms on campuses like Cornell

Michael Tracey, an independent journalist and commentator, posted on Friday what he said was the accuser's name, which Reuters was unable to verify, before quickly deleting it, saying his point had been ⁠made.

He has expressed sympathy for the accused men over what he says is the harassment they have faced and described his effort to name the Cornell accuser as journalistic diligence protected under the U.S. Constitution as free speech.

blocks.text: He told Reuters on Sunday ‌that he did not wish to encourage threats or harassment against the woman.

"The point, from my perspective, was more about the public-policy implications of this increasingly commonly used tactic in civil litigation, for plaintiffs' attorneys to introduce sensational, reputation-harming allegations using the cloak of anonymity for their clients," Tracey said in an interview.
N.Y. governor appoints special prosecutor to Cornell sexual assault case

Cornell University president ​Michael Kotlikoff said in a video message on Saturday that the university will examine the role of fraternities and sororities on campus following the outcry over the ⁠school's handling of the rape allegations.

"At their best, these organizations can provide students with friendship, belonging, mentorship and a ⁠powerful sense of community," he said. "But being part of a group can never diminish individual responsibility."
Since the lawsuit was ⁠filed last ⁠month, prosecutors in New York's Tompkins County have ​been criticized for their initial handling of the allegations in 2024.

blocks.text: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul last week named state Attorney ​General Letitia James as special prosecutor ⁠to look into the case.

U.S. President Donald Trump, a critic of James for years, lambasted the decision to appoint her. "And I feel badly for whoever she's looking at because they won't get a fair shake," he told reporters on Friday.
Asked about Trump's comment, Giuffra said the case shouldn't be politicized. "It has nothing to do with politics," he said.
